claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy forms a porous, non-protective oxide layer during high-temperature exposure.
Aluminum-rich pack cementation followed by heat treatment can form a uniform, adherent alumina scale on the alloy surface.
The aluminum-based surface treatment can significantly improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The treatment produces a continuous, dense, and well-adherent alumina layer.
At high temperature, aluminum from the coating reacts with oxygen to form alumina.
Alumina is a stable, slow-growing oxide at high temperature.
The alumina scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the alumina scale limits further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Under exposure at approximately 1100°C in air or pure oxygen for 100 hours, the treatment should improve oxidation resistance.
Treated samples should exhibit at least a 30% reduction in oxidation-related weight gain relative to untreated samples.
Treated samples should exhibit better surface-scale integrity than untreated samples.
Under identical exposure conditions, untreated samples develop more porous and less protective oxide scales than treated samples.
Under identical exposure conditions, untreated samples experience greater oxidation-related weight gain than treated samples.
The protective mechanism should be effective from approximately 1000°C to 1200°C.
Alumina remains stable over the approximately 1000°C to 1200°C range.
At lower temperatures, incomplete alumina-scale formation may diminish the treatment benefit.
At temperatures or conditions that cause scale spallation, the treatment benefit may diminish.
